# Plan DAG

**Performance rule for every code agent (the author's order of 2026-11-05).** Every agent that writes or changes code must pass a performance test showing that the code is O(1), O(n) or O(n log n), or O(n log N) where O(n) is not possible (the author's decision of 2026-11-04). It may not exhibit O(n²) or worse without the author's explicit approval. An agent that finds such a cost must look for a better solution first, and if it cannot find one, must ask the author what to do. An item is not done until this holds. This rule applies to every item before Zed0 and after it, and no item has an edge for it. The test runs at n and 8n with inputs built before timing and stays within 24x, and a negative control that is run but not committed shows that it fails on a slower version. Code that is obviously O(1) instead carries a `// O(1):` comment giving the reason. The item SCALE-cover delivers the tool that fails the local test suite when code has neither.

This file lists the remaining work on Zed and the order it must run in. It has 3738 items, 3584 edges and 120 levels (0 to 119). It covers the TODO items, the store fixes, the left-recursion work, the T14 and T11 findings and every unchecked step in `../zed/PROGRESS.md`.

**Needs relaxed on 2026-11-02.** Items now run in parallel in their own worktrees, and a merge resolves a small overlap in a file. So the `needs` column keeps only three kinds of edge: code (one item uses or changes code the other writes), measure (one item measures code the other changes) and files-heavy (both rewrite the same functions). Edges of the other kinds were dropped: files-light (the same file, different functions), order (a preferred order with no technical cause), docs (one item only reads the other's text) and none (no reason found). Of the 1134 edges classified, 907 were code, 109 measure, 13 files-heavy, 52 files-light, 35 order, 3 docs and 15 none. Where the reviewer of the classification disagreed, its judgment was used. T11-fix was split into T11-fix-store and T11-fix-rest, X14 was added, and edges found missing were added after reading the cited code.

## How to read it

- An edge means one item needs another. The item in the first column cannot start until every id in its `needs` column is merged.
- The level of an item is the length of the longest path from a root, where a root is an item with no needs. Level 0 holds the roots.
- Two items with no directed path between them, in either direction, may run in parallel. Two items at the same level never have a path between them.
- Levels are a convenience. Items at different levels can also be unordered, and may then run in parallel. Use the `needs` column, not the level number, to decide.
- A file conflict is one item's path equal to, or inside a directory of, the other's. Since 2026-11-02 a file conflict between two items that the DAG does not order no longer forces an order: both may run, and the merge resolves the overlap. Run them apart where possible. The conflict lists compare paths as written, so they do not show a conflict through a glob, such as `tests/steps/*/scaling.rs` (T2 and SCALE-cover).
- An edge is added only when the code, a measurement or a rewrite of the same functions requires it. A missing edge of that kind costs a bad merge; an edge for a light file overlap costs parallel time and is left out.
- Reasons for the edges are in [Why each item waits](#why-each-item-waits). Where a reason or note disagrees with the `needs` column, the `needs` column wins, since the notes were written before the corrections below.

**Done, so not listed:** T1 (all crates optimized in dev builds, `Cargo.toml` `[profile.dev]` at `opt-level = 2`) and T8 (code in other languages removed). Both landed in commit cd2d30b. Every step L1.1 to L1.39 and M0.x is also done, so a need on one of them is treated as met and left out of the table. The exceptions are L1.17a, L1.29a, L1.37a, L1.39a and L1.39b, added on 2026-11-03, which have rows.

**Files every step touches:** `tests/Cargo.toml` (written by the step_targets tool), `tests/steps/m0_01_scaffolding/`, `STATUS.md`, `COMPLEXITY.md` and `../zed/PROGRESS.md`. These are left out of the conflict lists, since every pair would match. The changes are additive, so resolve them at merge by keeping both sides, then rerun step_targets and regenerate `PROGRESS.md`. Each step's own `tests/steps/lNN_MM_*/` directory is separate from every other step's.

**Builders of new forms.** A builder tells kids apart by the token that follows or by position, never by rule name where a `~` rule can stand (STATUS.md, the LR4 fix).

First an inventory, kept in this row's notes file `docs/fp-ops-inventory.md`: the standard operations of the list and map libraries of Haskell (Data.List, Data.Map), OCaml (List, Map) and Scala (collections), each matched to the word DESIGN gives it (zipWith is `a.zip(b).map(…)`, filter is `.where`, a sum is `m >< (+)`), with its DESIGN step. An operation with no word in DESIGN goes into QUESTIONS.md with a proposed spelling, not into the code. Then build: `.any`, `.all`, `.find` (step L3.15a); count, min, max, sum and product as folds; `split`, `lines`, `concat` (step L3.2); `++` and `zip` (step L5.2); `scan` and `.chunkBy` (step L5.3); `sort` and `.orderedValues` with `asc`/`desc` keys, and `take(k)` (step L5.1); the reverse of an order (step L5.1c); `.first`/`.last`; and every other word the inventory finds in DESIGN. Each is written in Zed in the prelude over the kernel forms (`fam`, `discard`, `reindex`, `gen`, `fold`) wherever Zed can express it at the same cost, and is built in only with the reason stated here and in MAP-pure-zed. Kernel pieces have one owner each: MAP-run owns `fam`, `discard`, the identity `reindex`, the serial `gen` and `fold`; REMAP-run owns the general `reindex` and `group`; this row owns ranks, the sorted view (step L3.4) and scans. U` that must ride through `reindex` unchanged, faces table of sec:type_language). | 45 | L6.13g | Step L6.13g (DESIGN sec:memory "Edits by position", zed 12375bc and 52e4248): a wave of `splice` in place, or on a tree shared with the old version, natively (revised by XR-collection-edits). Reuse at count 1, per node, covers the wave, proved at compile time where the old version has no later reader, tested at run time otherwise; a function in the delta that reads the old version counts as its reader; on a flat array one pass moves each kept entry whose position changes once (those whose position falls in increasing order, then those whose position rises in decreasing order), leaves the others, writes the inserts into the gaps, the allocation grown first; a delta not in key order sorted first, O(k log k). Representation by the cost model, never a size constant: a level already a tree takes its waves on the tree; a single wave on a flat level with no remaining reader uses the pass; with a remaining reader, independent reads moved before the wave (L6.13b), then conversion to a tree whose leaves are slices of the old array (O(n/B) nodes, no entry copied by the conversion; a wave then rebuilds each touched leaf the old version still shares, once); in a loop, flat or tree by the waves' share `k / n`, the number of leaves their edits touch (n/64 edits in one run cost the tree 0.06 of the pass in the CD sweep, spread edits 1.4 times) and the reads between waves, the switchover measured on both sides in `benches/` `crossover` (author decision A96, as POLY-crossover-bench; the XR-collection-edits CD sweep found it between k/n = 1/128 and 1/64 in counted operations for leaves of 64, and a timed C prototype in round 2 near 1/1500 in elapsed time, so the benchmark counts the instructions the compiled code runs on each target, as sec:plan says of every A96 benchmark, not abstract operations, at several n, by the reads per wave; whether time decides where the two sides differ in cache misses is row SPEC-crossover-time) and recorded in COMPLEXITY.md; a tree whose older versions are released flattened by the same model, not at every release (flattening at each release is O(n²) over a loop of n one-edit waves; DESIGN states this departure from P319's wording); set/update-only levels stay flat where every entry takes one width in storage (L6.13b's saved entries for old readers), while on a `Utf8String` or `Utf16String` a `#set` that changes a code point's width moves the later units, so such waves take the pass and the cost model as inserts do (SPEC-L6-13g-width-change-waves). | 0 | SUB-fork-place-512 | Done by bundle-kernel5 (2026-11-17, 197c7de2b): option (a) built in general. `Search::least_height` (Knuth's generalization of Dijkstra's algorithm) and `Search::value_height` let `member_known` refute a value lower than its type's least height or higher than its greatest in O(1); `Search::height_bounds` (Tarjan's algorithm for the cycles) bounds the heights of a type's values, and `Searching::empty` finds a type whose height range is empty at once, so R_a ∩ R_b of two exact lengths is decided without walking `min(a, b)` levels (263,783 types at n 512 before, 8,190 after). Proofs at the functions; unit tests in `types/empty/tests.rs` (exact bounds on 15 types; every value found for 414 types lies within its type's bounds). Both l01_23 benchmarks now run at 64 and 512: 7.99 and 8.09 times the instructions (load 47). Negative control, not committed: without the empty range, 32.35 times, fails. COMPLEXITY.md K126. Earlier text: given back by bundle-kernel4 (2026-11-17), size L: cause found, not fixed. Profile: perf's DWARF unwinding failed because lld links with `--rosegment`, which the libdw unwinder of perf 7.3.3 does not handle (zrun is not the cause); built with `RUSTFLAGS="-C link-arg=-Wl,--no-rosegment"` and recorded with `perf record --call-graph dwarf,32768 --user-callchains` inside zrun, the call chains unwind. Cause: `verdict_alone` (`types/empty.rs`) runs three searches on these types: the strict search with forks refused (it stops at the fork), `empty_past_forks` (false), then `Search { strict: true, open_forks: true }.rep(self)`. The third is Θ(n²): it makes 3,047 types and 1,393 regions at n = 64 and 263,783 types and 130,865 regions at n = 512, and `Search::rep` is 42.7% of the run at 512, 56 times its time at 64. It meets one candidate list of exact length (R34) with each of the n arms G_i of `list_named(int) - by_place_from_the_end(n)`, and each meet R_a ∩ R_b of two exact lengths is decided one level at a time, a chain of new types as long as the list: at n = 56, 759 types `(#cons (& (tuple int R) (tuple int R) (tuple int L)))`, about 33 an arm. The counts jump between neighboring n because the arms are met in digest order. `is_empty` itself is linear in count (641 to 5,122 regions, 8 times); its extra 1.68 times is cost per operation: self-time ratios from 64 to 512 of 110 for `member_known` (2.1% of the run), 54.5 for its frame closure, 65 for the `HashMap<(usize, Type), Option<bool>>` memo, 36 for `name_digest`, 30 for the usize equivalence. Fix options, none built: (a) decide R_a ∩ R_b empty for two exact lengths a ≠ b in O(1) from a length summary of each list type, before the meet level by level; (b) test the third search's candidate against the whole union in one walk rather than one meet per arm; (c) reuse the strict search's work in the open-forks search. Each changes the search in `empty.rs` and needs its own proof that no verdict changes. Filed by bundle-kernel3 (2026-11-17): after SUB-empty-fork-bytes (the seed skips excluded rows, COMPLEXITY.md K126) the l01_23 benchmarks `refusals::bench::emptiness_counts_a_fork_as_inhabited_in_its_size` and `a_union_of_lists_by_the_place_of_a_one_is_refused_in_its_size` pass from n 8 to 64 (8.30 and 9.97 times the instructions), but one size step more, n 64 to 512, costs 13.4 and 35.1 times the bytes (load 38), the second about as before the change. Building `list_named(int) - by_place_from_the_end(n)` alone is linear there (8.7 times the instructions, 8.3 times the bytes), so the growth is in the decision. A perf profile with dwarf call chains did not unwind inside zrun (flat profile only: allocation, the `Bucket<Set<Row>>` and `Cell` tables, the `(u64, u64, Cut)` memo); count calls by phase, as bundle-kernel2 did for the seed, then bring the 64 to 512 step under 10.5 (under 9 preferred) and check it in the two tests. Was: given back by bundle-kernel4 (2026-11-17), size L: the root index below was built and fails another benchmark. Built as refinements (1) and (2) say: a join-based treap with sizes (Blelloch, Ferizovic and Sun; Seidel and Aragon), labels from 2^62 with a new front block taking the least label less one, the new root's index derived in `replace` in O(log m) expected, and the cut in `or_literal` keeping the label prefix with stale atom entries above every label. The rejoin test, moved to `bdd/bench.rs` (TEST-bench-move), passed at 512 and 4096 with 9.83 times the instructions and 9.9 times the bytes (HEAD: 10.75 and 10.7, red). Negative controls failed as they should: with no index carried, over 60 s; with a join that does not remap the other blocks' atoms, 4 correctness tests. But `types::bdd::bench::a_long_meet_joined_to_short_meets_scales` went from 13.1 s (9.28 times, HEAD) to over 60 s. The old summaries sat on left children and were shared by every list that shares those cells, and the root's own block needed none; the root index is lost by every root made other than by `replace` (`Bdd::assemble`, `merge`, `split_parts`, and `set::difference_if_agree` in `zip_chain`), so the next `find` builds it over all k atoms. In that benchmark 5,163 indexes of 16,383 atoms were built in 20 s, one a zip: O(m²) in all. Still needed: a summary shared across lists as the old one is but O(1) a level, or an index that survives the constructors that make fresh roots (carrying it through `merge` needs relabeling one side, O(size)). The attempt (diffs, `treap.rs` and its tests) is kept in /home/luke/Work/wt/scratch/KERNEL-bdd-rejoin-bytes-root-index/. Given back by bundle-kernel3 (2026-11-17), size M: the label method below confirmed as the one that removes a log, with two refinements. (1) Keep the labels and the atom-to-label map on the root cell, made on first use in a `OnceLock` as `atoms` is, so the cells' hash-consing and equality do not see them; that data describes the cell's sequence, so it is valid whatever edits made the cell, and `or_literal` derives the new root's data from the old root's in O(log m) (one map update, one label for a new front block), building it in O(m) only for a root that has none. (2) `find(a)` is then one map lookup for the label of a's block and one descent by label to the block whose label is the greatest at or below it, checked by `set::get`; its place comes from the sizes on that descent. Rejected: an `imbl::HashSet` summary in place of the `OrdSet` (a HAMT is O(log m) deep in base 32 for m uniform hashes, so still O(log² m) per literal with a smaller constant; no proof meets 10.5). Literature (allpapers search, 2026-11-17): Dietz and Sleator order maintenance; "Order Maintenance in Worst-Case Constant Time, Verified"; "On-line Indexing for General Alphabets via Predecessor Queries on Subsets of an Ordered List"; Blelloch, Ferizovic and Sun, "Parallel Ordered Sets Using Join" (join-based treaps with sizes, also needed by CHECK-literal-union-cost). Given back by bundle-kernel2 (2026-11-17), size M, not S. The bound is `O(log² m)` comparisons per literal in expectation, now stated in COMPLEXITY.md K67 (4): `Cell::find` tests an `imbl::OrdSet` summary, `O(log m)` comparisons, at each of `O(log m)` levels, and `carry` updates one summary per rebuilt left child. The ratio is the n log² n one in the limit: 10.73 at 512 to 4096 (n log n predicts 10.67 there, n log² n 14.2) but 11.22 at 4096 to 32,768 (n log n 10.0, n log² n 12.5), so a proof cannot meet 10.5 and a log must go. Method needed, not built here since it changes the one form of a list: find an atom's block without a summary per level, e.g. order the treap by a label per block (a new front block takes the first label less one; a block edited or joined in place keeps a label of the blocks it replaces) and keep one persistent map from atom to label at the root, checked against the block found, so `find` is one map lookup and one descent of O(1) comparisons a level; the labels must stay out of the cells' hash-consing and equality. Was: partly done by bundle-kernel1 (39fe21930, 2026-11-17): `or_literal` carries atom summaries only into left children and does not look again for an atom it removed; 512 to 4096 blocks now 10.73 times the instructions (11.55 before) and 10.90 times the bytes (11.7 before), still over 10.5, so the test stays deferred. Round 2 (author 2026-11-13 18:16: no fixed sequence of stages; a provable theory with rules that give each program one partial ordering): DESIGN sec:checking_in_zed, "Checks and evaluations on one dependency graph". The nodes are facts, not definitions; iterable facts (types, bounds, derived facets) are solved by strongly connected component, once facts (verdicts, evaluations, compiled regions) read one node at a time, as they run, and run once on final values; rules 1 to 6; the meaning independent of order (closure, then refusal of the components of the wait graph that wait on nothing outside them); the partial ordering is the reachability order of the components of the final read graph. Engine `zedc_lattice::schedule` (`zedc::store::schedule`): one iterative Tarjan search, proved at the code to end, to give one result for every order of roots and numbering (a single-file check agrees with the build) and to run each once fact on the most precise values; checked against an independent implementation of the meaning on 1500 random programs; 7.96 times the instructions and 8.00 times the bytes at 8n. The keyed write `main::files["x"] <- v` from a helper has no cycle per fact (tested on the model; reads of `main::files` from a helper already compile, MAIN-files, and the write itself is L7.2). zedc does not call the engine yet: SCHED-scc-unit, SCHED-eval-before-check, SCHED-refined-store, SCHED-schema-types. | - | - | none | `crates/zedc-lattice/src/schedule.rs`, `tests/steps/m0_05_widening_and_iteration/schedule.rs` |

Was: Author 2026-11-14 (P162), verbatim: "require that all foreign function bindings that depend upon holding a library open or holding a setup state non-released depend upon a value form the setup, even if internally the binding does nothing with the passed value and calls the C library without it. In DESIGN sec:ffi ("A library's state is a token", "You can't access the resource without the token") and sec:diagnostics: make the token parameter required, not optional. Fix: the text is cut at NFC composition boundaries (UAX #15, "Stable Code Points"): before a character whose decomposition starts with a starter of quick check Yes, or a starter of quick check Maybe that does not compose with the last character of NFC of the piece so far; the span is the first piece that is not NFC. The proposed fix (grow the span while NFC of span and next piece changes) was not used: it needs the same boundary test to stop and costs O(N²) on a long run of pieces. | 0 | DOC-port-in-bound-errors | Found by TEST-types-unreached-paths: DESIGN.md L1.22 says only "`Lines` and `Files` are port types, not types of values, so `is` rejects them", and does not say which errors stand when a bounded function type `L .. U -> V` holds a port. The checker gives only the port error when the port is in a bound (`x is (Lines .. int -> int)`: the bounds are not compared), and both errors, the bounds error first, when the port is in `V` (`x is (#a \| #c .. #a \| #b -> Lines)`). Both are pinned by tests/steps/l01_22_type_representation/complete.rs `is_rejects_a_port_in_an_intersection_a_difference_and_a_bound` and `a_bounds_error_and_a_port_error_both_stand_in_written_order`. Decide by the standing rules (explicit, no surprises; most likely: a bound that denotes no type cannot be compared, so the bounds error is left out, while a port in `V` leaves the bounds comparable), write the sentence into DESIGN L1.22 with the grammar tools rerun, and change the tests if the decision differs. Only if the rules cannot decide it, add a QUESTIONS entry and block this row on it | S | no | none | DESIGN.md L1.22, `tests/steps/l01_22_type_representation/complete.rs` |

Cause (traced): fits_slot and why_unfit (crates/zedc-check/src/check/walk.rs) checked needs only when the passed signature itself had them, so a function returning one with needs went to `fits_in`, whose solved path (crates/zedc-types/src/ty.rs) fits a signature with needs only to an equal one. | 0 | FAIL-returned-chain-quadratic | Done: 73afa198e "FAIL-returned-chain-quadratic: a chain of n functions each returning the one before is checked in linear time"; no spec change. Cause (traced with gdb samples): `Ck::finish` called `finished` for each definition, and `finished` ran `sig_vars` and `renamed(..).replace(..)` over the whole signature; each `ri` is `i` arrows deep and still holds `w`'s class variable, so the checker walked and rebuilt the chain whole for every definition. Fix: `Sig::vars_order` (crates/zedc-types/src/ty.rs) keeps the variable order of a signature once it is asked for, and the `vars_of` walk reads a kept order at a held function or enters it once per walk; `Renamings` keeps the rename and replace memos across the signatures of one `finish`. Chain 57.3 times before, 7.88 after (31.4M to 247.3M instructions); curried lambdas 8.42 and deep bounded 8.55, unchanged. A first design, an order kept at every function, was rejected: curried lambdas 60.4 times and 66.5 GB | S | no | none | `crates/zedc-types/src/ty.rs`, `crates/zedc-check/src/check/mod.rs`, `tests/steps/l01_26_type_resolution/bench/held_functions.rs` |

| 0 | FAIL-types-overload-bounded-tuple | Done: the commit "FAIL-types-overload-bounded-tuple: ..." that marks this row Done; no spec change. The inferred cause was right: `Comparing::search` gives a tuple piece to the first shape of `s` in written order that holds it, and `accepts` bound the first variable it found, so `(U,)` bound `B` (`for B in int \| f64`) in `(B,)`, which `bounds_hold` then refused. Fix (root cause, no third shortcut): `accepts` binds a variable only to a piece its bound holds, checked as `bounds_hold` checks it (`Binds::bound`, a binary search of the signature's bounds, shared by every copy of the binding; `var_mask`, `carrier_of`), so the shape does not hold the piece and the search goes on to `(U,)`. Only a piece known to lie outside the bound is refused: a carrier outside it, a variable of a known mask outside it (rigid, or a bounded own variable of an open comparison, `Cx::own_bounds`); a free or unbounded variable is checked as before. Outside every tuple shape (`Site::Other`) no other shape is searched, so a piece no variable admits is bound as before and `bounds_hold` names that binding in its message. `Cx::open` gives `s` its bounds under the names it reads them by. A rigid variable whose mask is one carrier counts as that carrier (`carrier_of`), so `T` bound to `V \| int` for `V in int` is one carrier. The two shortcuts of d20413aae (`read_alike`, `equal_fits`) stay: with either switched off a test fails (`a_bounded_variable_is_bound_only_to_what_its_bound_holds`, `signatures_with_a_variable_bound_in_a_tuple_fit_themselves_and_their_overloads`), each on an unbounded variable in the first shape, which a bound does not decide (row FAIL-types-first-shape-unbounded); this row's test passes with both off. Tests in `crates/zedc-types/src/ty.rs` (`an_overload_with_a_bounded_variable_fits_where_one_of_its_arrows_is_expected` and three neighbors, outer variables, function types and class variables included) and `tests/steps/l01_26_type_resolution/bounds.rs` (`a_bounded_variable_beside_a_free_one_takes_only_what_its_bound_holds`, red on the base); benchmark `bench::bounds::a_signature_of_many_bounded_variables_beside_a_free_one_fits_in_time_near_its_size` 8.17x (COMPLEXITY.md). Found while testing the untested cases: rows FAIL-types-own-same-name, FAIL-types-payload-vars-unread, FAIL-types-first-shape-unbounded. | S | no | none | `crates/zedc-types/src/ty.rs` |

Cause (traced; the inferred cause was right): `Cx::read` (base 5d9bad32b) read the variables and functions of a type's tuples and left its atoms' payloads as written, so the `C` of `q`'s `#p(C)`, read as a rigid name under a new name elsewhere (`Cx::open`), kept its written name in the payload; `Comparing::payloads_in` then bound the `B` of `s` to that `C`, a variable of no known carrier, and `bounds_hold` refused. Fix: `Cx::read` reads payload shapes as it reads tuple rows, on one explicit stack, components in order (so the new names are made in the order the recursive form made them); a shape with no variable and no function (`ShapeData::fixed`) is not walked, and a shared shape is read once (a memo by its number); `read_outer` rebuilds the payloads from the shapes read. Benchmark `bench::bounds::signatures_of_many_free_or_bounded_variables_fit_themselves_renamed_in_time_near_their_size`, payload of n bounded variables at 2000 and 16000: 9.32x; negative control (the components of a shape collected again for each component, O(k^2) a shape) 30.8x. | 0 | FAIL-types-first-shape-unbounded | Done: the commit "FAIL-types-own-same-name, FAIL-types-first-shape-unbounded: ..." that marks this row Done; no spec change. Cause (traced): `arrow_fits` (base 531c58875) compares the parameters once, and `Comparing::search` gives each piece to the first shape that holds it, so a free variable `T` in the first shape takes `(W,)` or `(1,)`, and the result `(T,)` is then wider than `q`'s; nothing later undoes the binding. Fix, at the root and not a third shortcut: the result of `q` puts a ceiling on each free variable of `s` that stands alone at a place of `s`'s result (`ceilings`: `q`'s tuples grouped by length, each place joined once), and `accepts` binds such a variable only to a piece that may lie within its ceiling (`may_be_within`, `Binds::ceiling`), so the piece goes on to the next shape. A ceiling is a necessary condition only where the tuple holds a value, so where the comparison under ceilings fails, `arrow_fits` compares once more without them (at most two comparisons per arrow; nested verdicts are kept by `fits_read`); the free variables a parameter does not bind are read as `Never` (`Binds::of_arrow`), so `(x0: int \| T) -> T` fits `(x0: int) -> int`. The search stays first-fit: with three or more shapes of variables a second member of a union still cannot go to a later shape of the same bucket (F124), now row FAIL-types-three-variable-shapes. Shortcuts: `read_alike` stays: with it off, `a_signature_fits_itself` and `a_bounded_variable_is_bound_only_to_what_its_bound_holds` fail, each on a signature with a union of three shapes of variables compared with itself; with `equal_fits` off every test of l01_22, l01_26, zedc_types and zedc_check passes, and it stays as a fast path. Tests: `an_unbounded_variable_in_the_first_shape_does_not_take_every_piece` (ty.rs, with two-variable results and a `Never` row) and `free_variables_fit_themselves_under_other_names` (`tests/steps/l01_26_type_resolution/bounds.rs`, n = 1 to 4, both ways of each boundary), red on the base. Benchmark `bench::bounds::signatures_of_many_free_variables_fit_themselves_renamed_in_time_near_their_size` 8.63x; negative control (linear scan of `Cx::free`) 22.0x. The n-parameter form is quadratic before and after this change: row FAIL-types-binds-copied-per-shape. | S | no | none | `crates/zedc-types/src/ty.rs` |
| 0 | FAIL-types-three-variable-shapes | Done: the commit "FAIL-types-three-variable-shapes: ..." that marks this row Done; no spec change. Cause (traced): `Comparing::search` refuses a second member of a union that needs a shape of a bucket past one it failed (F124); with ceilings from the result, `(W,)` and `(Y,)` each failed `(T,)`. Fix: a bucket in which a member fails its first shape, where the binding has ceilings, has its shapes pinned (`Pins`): a shape whose component at some place is one variable `v` (neither rigid nor a function) with a ceiling `c` is filed there under `v` and each variable of `c`, and in `open` where `c` holds a scalar set, tuples or functions; a member is then tried on the free shapes and, at each pinned place, on the shorter of the shapes filed under its first variable there and those `open` where it holds a scalar, in written order (a heap over the lists). Proof at `Pins::lists`: a shape left out is refused by `accepts`, `admits` and `may_be_within` whatever the bindings so far. Second fix, a pre-existing flaw: `arrow_fits` took the false of the attempt with no ceilings as decided where the attempt within them was refused; the refusal is now kept. Departure from the row's proposal: no lookup of shapes already bound and no cursor; counts of members per canonical shape were not taken either, since an unbounded variable takes the union of the members it holds. Still refused: two members failing a shape no pin leaves out. `read_alike` stays (not measured with it off in this change). Tests (ty.rs): `n_shapes_of_variables_fit_themselves_renamed` (n = 1 to 8), `pinned_and_free_shapes_of_one_bucket_fit_themselves_renamed`, `shapes_that_take_more_members_than_the_result_holds_do_not_fit`, `shapes_that_share_a_variable_take_the_union_of_their_members`, `scalar_members_skip_shapes_pinned_by_ceilings_of_variables`, `a_signature_the_pins_do_not_separate_is_still_refused` (a case still given up), and the sweep `pinned_shapes_are_those_of_the_rule_of_one_shape` against `SCAN_ALL` (3000 random signatures; one run: 1290 held, 1707 failed, 3 refused). Benchmarks `l01_26_type_resolution::bench::scaling::n_shapes_of_variables_pinned_by_the_result_fit_themselves_renamed_in_linear_time` 8.62x and `n_pinned_shapes_of_variables_beside_scalars_fit_themselves_renamed_in_linear_time` 8.62x (n = 15,000 and 120,000). V` has L = {} and U = K, and `<:` holds iff L2 <: L1, U1 <: U2, V1 <: V2; "a wider exact domain is not a subtype of a narrower one: `int -> int` is not `<: int[0..<10] -> int`". DESIGN.md L1.26a says that under `==` and `!=` a literal operation follows the class without removing carriers from it, and `==` between an `int` and a value of another kind is false (the kernel's `number_eq`), so `y = f(3)` is `false` as the generic form gives; the declared `x: int` is refused by "exactly or not at all", as isBig is in L1.26a. Refusing the call at `int` would remove `int` from the class by a comparison, which L1.26a rules out, and the existing tests `param_follows` (`x == 4 / 2` is false at an int) fix the same answer. The generic and declared forms agree wherever both are accepted (`rat`, `f64`, `f32`); at `int` the declared form is refused and the generic one answers `false`, both as DESIGN gives. Tests in tests/steps/l01_26a_generic_literals/operations.rs: `an_int_compares_unequal_with_an_operation_that_holds_no_int`, `an_int_reaches_an_operation_that_holds_no_int_only_through_a_comparison`, and the `int` argument for the `==` and `!=` bodies of `operations_on_literals_give_each_carrier_s_value`; the comments of `without_int` (walk.rs) state the two claims and what tests them. One operation behaves differently at a generic parameter and at the type written out (DESIGN rule (2) of the design principles). Fix in zedc-check: refuse the call at `int` as at `f(positional x: int)` (L1.26a: `/` or a decimal among the literals takes `int` out of the witness's class, which the call must then not reach), or record per operation in `check::Info` whether `int` is left in the class so `without_int` keeps the stopping arm there. Cause (traced): `Comparing::search` gives each shape it tries a copy of the binding (`fit(r, binds.clone())`), and `Binds` held a `BTreeMap`, whose copy costs the size of the binding; the binding holds a variable for each parameter compared so far, so n parameters, each a union of two shapes, cost O(n^2). Fix: the map of `Binds` is persistent (`BindMap`, `imbl::OrdMap`, as `Env`; the set of class keys in `BindKeys` is an `imbl::OrdSet`): a copy is O(1), an insert into a copy O(log n). `Binds::values_mut` became `update_each` (the persistent map lends no mutable walk) and `retain` removes in a second pass. Undoing a failed shape's bindings was not taken: every writer of the binding would have to log its changes. Wrong yes: `p(f: (h: int, y: int) -> int) = f(h: 1, y: 2); q(g: (h: T, y: T) -> int) = p(f: g); s(h: bool, y: bool) = 0; a = q(g: s);` is accepted, so `p` calls `s` with two `int`s; also with `q(g: (h: T, y: T) -> int, z: T)` and `q(g: s, z: true)`. Inside `q` the class of `T` is held in `g`'s function type; when `g` is passed at `p`'s closed parameter the fit takes the class as `int`, but the class is neither narrowed nor recorded as a need. A direct call `g(h: 1, y: 2)` inside `q` narrows it, and a class passed directly is narrowed. The same with ty.rs before and after types12, so it predates that work. Inferred cause (not traced to the line): the call path in crates/zedc-check/src/check/walk.rs (`call_sig_step`, `instantiated`) restricts classes that are arguments, not classes held inside a function-typed argument. Fix: restrict each held class to what the fit took it as, or record it as a need. Also: the refusal of the nested variant prints `_` for the class ("`p` does not take ((h: (x: _) -> int, y: _) -> int)"), not a type the user can write. The code was wrong, the test right: a held memo entry was reused on a higher stack, where reading the term again can enter a lambda that is active there and raise a Recursion stop. In the seed, v241 = App(v229, ..) is read inside Lam v242; v229's body reaches #3 again, which applies Lam v242, so reading again stops on it and the entry did not (an experiment that refused every held entry on a higher stack passed the seed). An entry is now (value, cut, high): `high` is the stack height it was made at when its read entered a lambda (`Run::entered` counts them), else usize::MAX, and a hit is reused only on a stack no higher than `high`; a hit with a finite `high` counts as entering a lambda. The exact rule needs the set of lambdas each read entered, O(l) per entry; the flag is O(1) per read and costs no read more than before. Tests: `entries_made_below_a_stop_give_what_reading_the_term_again_gives_seed_17213863407132117863` (red before); 399 of 400 random seeds of the entries and summaries tests passed, the one failure FAIL-preimage-summaries-rounds-seed. l01_25 benches (scaling, stops, shared): 26 pieces pass, ratios 3.5 to 8.9 apart from the n-squared `x * y mod 7 == 3` (46.1, 64 times the points). The cause named above does not hold: zrun mounts each worktree's own build over the fixed target directory, so two worktrees never share `<target>/tmp`. Two causes inside one worktree do. (1) Two tests of one binary wrote one name with different texts, and `std::fs::write` empties a file before it fills it: in l01_19, `twice`, `untyped`, `string` and `default` were each written by two tests; the two tests that wrote `twice` (`ports::a_port_given_to_a_helper_is_still_pushed_once`, `writes::a_port_pushed_twice_in_one_wave_is_an_error`), run together in one process 300 times one after another, failed 185 of 300 runs at the base and 0 of 300 after. (2) tools/run_tests.sh runs several processes of one binary at once, all in one `<target>/tmp` (TEST-fixture-write-race). New module `tests/src/scratch.rs` (re-exported by `step_helpers`): `process_tmpdir()` gives each running process of a test binary a directory of its own, `<target>/tmp/<binary>/process-<k>`, the first slot whose lock (`flock`) no running process holds; slots are kept from run to run, never emptied, because `zed_native::link::kept` finds the executables linked there by the last run (emptying them would link each again, about 1.5 s each). `scratch(path)` gives a test a path in it and panics when a second test of the process names the same path (libtest names each test's thread after the test, also with one test thread), so a shared name fails every run instead of now and then. It found the four l01_19 names; it also flags the directories `one_engine` and `sites` of l01_36a, which several tests used with files of distinct names (no race, but the guard works per path), so each test there now has a directory of its own. 4 new tests in `tests/src/scratch_tests.rs`; zed-tests lists 60 tests, was 56. Fix: `decide` and `satisfiable` first write `f` one way, `signed(f, Signs::Free)`: each row divided by the common factor of its coefficients, each equation with the sign `flips` chooses from its coefficients or constant, `t >= 0` beside `-t >= 0` joined into `t == 0`; an equation whose sign only the names would choose (`a - b == 0`), and such a pair, stay as written, since choosing by name made the answer depend on the naming (l01_38 names, seed 16475671021983193007 system 6: 12 namings Ok(true), 12 Unordered; test `a_joined_equation_whose_sign_only_the_names_choose_gives_one_answer`, red with the sign chosen by name); holding both signs of such an equation instead was measured and rejected (cell_sweep and r5 hull and orbit benchmarks 2 to 4 times slower, six of them past their time limit); nodes already written so keep their ids, so the solver's memos still find them. Cost O(n log n) in the size of `f`; to keep it near the cost of the solve, `Joining` finds equal rows through an `FxHashMap` of a hash of each row's terms (it copied each row's terms into a `BTreeMap` key, 228 ms of 267 ms on 38,000 equations) and `flips` compares one sorted list of references (it copied two). | 86 | HOST-embed | QUESTIONS Q38, answered by the author 2026-11-14 (zed commit 75cfe63; read the answer verbatim there): a C program drives a stateful Zed program directly. `@export` of such a program gives three C symbols: allocate (makes the state), tick (takes that state, a double pointer to a result and a result code saying whether the Zed function returned of its own accord before the C side called release) and release (frees the state; idempotent). Inside Zed the tick function takes an input stream and an output stream and does not return between ticks: its state is kept as a continuation and it yields to C each time its loop over the input stream waits for the next item. Results the output stream gives are allocated with malloc and freed by the C caller; the result pointer is set to null when a tick gives nothing. When the Zed function returns, its release runs at once and further ticks are invalid; after a release from C, further ticks are invalid. Do: (1) the sec:ffi paragraph beside the exports paragraph, with spec/grammar sync if `@export` syntax changes, and the sec:alternatives row correcting the Murail study's reason; (2) settle in DESIGN whether the result code is the tick's return value or an out-parameter, make a tick after release a defined, reported error (every catchable runtime error is caught), name the result type and its free function in the generated header, and state how the two streams meet the dynamic ports of Q51; (3) build it in libzed (no Rust after S.8); (4) tests: a C host allocates, ticks one item at a time and compares every output with the interpreter, the Zed side returning early (result code set, automatic release, tick after it refused), release called twice, release with no tick, a tick giving nothing (null result), results holding struct graphs freed by C under a leak checker. Added by the author the same day: `@export` names the path of a C header file to generate, and that header defines every struct of the object graphs the output stream can allocate and return (with the three functions and the result type); test that the header compiles with `cc -std=c11 -Wall -Werror` and that a host built only from it frees every result graph without a leak. Added by the author the same day (P195): every tick function compiles two ways. (a) The exported version, in the shared library with the C interface: its input-stream readers read the C caller's struct graphs in place and never free them, and the graphs it writes to the output stream are plain C layouts with no refcounts, written once in that form (no second copy made to strip refcounts). (b) When Zed code in the same program calls the tick function directly, a second version is compiled under Zed's normal refcounting and its stream fusion (state-machine or coroutine compilation), with the input stream fused to the caller and the output stream to the consumer, so no buffer or C graph is built. Both versions come from one definition and must agree: test each tick function both ways on the same inputs, comparing output values and counting allocations (the fused version allocates nothing the unfused one does not, and the exported one does no refcount operation). Scheduled late at the author's request. Added 2026-11-17 (FFI-cexport, author P380): the header, the free functions and the C layouts come from FFI-cexport's generator and type table (DESIGN sec:ffi, "A library compiled to a C library"), which this row extends with the three tick symbols | L | no | S.8, FFI-cexport | `DESIGN.md` sec:ffi, libzed FFI layer, tests |

Leads: Blelloch, Ferizovic and Sun, "Parallel Ordered Sets Using Join" (SPAA 2016: split, join, union and difference on treaps with sizes) and PAM, "Parallel Augmented Maps" (Sun, Ferizovic and Blelloch), the reference join-based treap; `types/bdd/settings.rs` already holds a join-based treap after that paper, but keyed by `Key<A>` and without sizes, so a set of `Value` with sizes is new code, and could serve as the label sequence of KERNEL-bdd-rejoin-bytes too. Given back by bundle-kernel2 (2026-11-17), size M, not S: no persistent ordered set in the repository splits in O(log k). `Lits::values` is an `imbl::OrdSet` (imbl 7.0.2), whose `split` and `split_member` go through `OrdMap::split_lookup`, a fold that inserts every element into two new maps (`imbl-7.0.2/src/ord/map.rs` line 1381, with the upstream comment "this is atrociously slow"), so O(k log k) a split with nothing shared; the treaps in the repository (`bdd.rs` module `list`, `zedc-preimage` `divisors.rs`, `zedc-lattice` `interval.rs`) are each made for their own contents, none a set of `Value`. Method needed: a join-based persistent treap of `Value` with sizes (split and join O(log k), union and difference O(m log(n/m + 1)) for m ≤ n) as the set of `Lits`, every reader of `Lits::values` moved to it; and the arrow results of a callee joined once per signature in `walk::read_at`, not once per test. Was: partly done by bundle-kernel1 (07647f17f, 2026-11-17): benchmark `l01_39_reduced_product::arm_test_through_call::bench::a_callee_of_k_literal_arms_scales`, one callee of k nested literal arms at 512 and 4096, passes at 8.0 times the instructions and 8.1 times the bytes, with no code change. Open: k tests `if f(x) > c { 1 } else { 0 }` on that callee cost O(k²), 34.6 times the instructions from 32 to 256 and 45.0 from 64 to 512. A temporary count (not committed) at k = 64 found 548 joins of about 65 literals from three sites a test: `walk::read_at` re-joins the callee's arrow results (`Ty::union_all(sig.arrows...)`, 3 a test), `Product::reduce_domains` relists the bound type's ints and joins them (4 a test), `Scope::reduce_with` (about 1.5 a test). Each test's narrowed type also holds about k/2 literals, so O(k log k) in all needs literal sets that split in O(log k) and share structure; size M. Found by CHECK-spine-tests-per-body (2026-11-14) while it made its benchmark: k tests on a name bound to a callee of k nested arms each giving a literal (`{ j }`) took about 18 times the wall time at 8 times k (debug, load about 50), where arms `{ x + j }` took 6.4 times; the profile put the time in the types of unions of literals (`Lits::union`, `Lits::insert`, `zip`, `Value::cmp`, `number_cmp`), not in reading the calls. The benchmark uses `x + j` arms for that reason. | 0 | PRES-switchover-not-race | Done: (the commit "PRES-switchover-not-race: the join of row sums runs first under a fixed work limit, ..." and the commit that marks this row Done). The race (Levin's universal search) is removed. The join of row sums runs first, alone, under the fixed work limit `JOIN_LIMIT` (2·10^7 units of its own work, charged before each operation, so a stop falls at the same point on every run); past it `decide` and `satisfiable` ask the solver, whose answers there are the same, and `project_each` refuses with the new `Refusal::Work` rather than give the solver's union of hulls (P197: refuse rather than answer coarser). A range is added by doubling with the table settled into intervals after each doubling, and a point takes each sum apart by the intervals of the table before it (`least_step`). Measured (Ryzen 9 5950X, load 40-56, best of three, `l01_38_presburger::bench::disj_groups::switchover`, COMPLEXITY.md Crossovers): 4.27 to 10.68 ns per unit on cases of at least 10^6 units, so the limit is at most 214 ms (A99 allows 250 ms); a stop took 182-201 ms. Before: the race took 1.1-1.8 s to decide `wide` k = 32 and 7-9 s for its point; now 0.30 ms and 0.31 ms. The one family where the solver is faster is `sparse` (weights far apart): k = 2, m = 10^4 join 9.3 ms against the solver's 0.066 ms; m = 10^6 the join stops after about 200 ms, then the solver answers; there the default path is slower than the solver alone by up to the limit's time (PRES-join-cost-predictor). Original row: Author 2026-11-14 (P196): "I certainly never would have asked for a race between two solutions. You must find a way to prove whether a fast path is possible, yielding the correct result in much less time, or when the full solver is needed. (Ideally, most or all cases should have a fast path, except for rare cases, which can be handled by the full solver, and as always, pathological cases that will provably blow up must be rejected by similar criteria but different thresholds.) Reason through where the switchovers from fast path to full solver to refusal should happen, based on which metrics. And as with all switchover logic, you need to actually measure this so that you can tell if your switchover heuristic is sound for the current CPU target, and document it as needing to be measured on other targets. A decimal literal that no use fixes takes f64 (reverses the 2026-11-09 rejection); an integer literal that no use fixes stays `int`, so `1 / 2`, `2 ^ -1` and `(3/2) ^ -2` with nothing fixing them stay refused, the exact repair first (`1r / 2`, `2r ^ -1`, `(3r / 2) ^ -2`), then the f64 one (`1.0 / 2`). A use that fixes a carrier fixes it for the literal, as for every literal since 2026-11-09: `r: rat = 0.5 ^ n` is accepted and exact, as `r: rat = 0.5` is (CHANGES the author request to refuse it; the repair `0.5r ^ n` is instead offered where an f64 `y = 0.5 ^ n` meets a rat use); `f: f32 = 0.5 ^ n` is f32. The exponent of `^` is the one exception to the rule that both operands of an arithmetic operation have one carrier: an `int` exponent goes with a base of any number carrier, `(int, int) -> int` (exponent proved non-negative), `(rat, int) -> rat`, `(F, int) -> F` at every float format F; a non-integer exponent needs one carrier, so the repair for a `rat` exponent `k` is `f64(x) ^ f64(k)`, and for a float one `f64(x) ^ k`; an int base literal beside a decimal exponent takes f64 (`2 ^ 0.5` is f64, no refusal). (5) Typing by value (POW-rat-literal-ops) narrows the result within an arrow and never creates one: `4r ^ 0.5r` is refused as any rat ^ non-integer is; `0.0 ^ -1` and `1.0 / 0.0` written with literals alone are `inf` by item (3) as changed, so no always-atom error (was: they yield only `#divByZero`, a compile error by the always-atom rule); every repair printed is run through `zedc run` | M | no | POW-rat-literal-ops | `DESIGN.md`, `crates/zedc-check/src/check/walk.rs`, `crates/zed-kernel/src/eval.rs`, `crates/zedc-lattice/src/float.rs` |

| 0 | SPEC-zero-order | DESIGN L1.17 orders numbers by exact value, then kind, then float format, and sec:order says a natural order's ties are exactly ==; so -0.0 and 0.0 (one rational, one format, -0.0 == 0.0) get one place. The kernel's natural order (crates/zed-kernel/src/value.rs:679-683 number_cmp, F64 Ord = total_cmp) puts -0.0 before 0.0, and must: Value's Eq is bitwise (the two zeros print differently and have different content addresses), and Rust's Ord must agree with Eq. Keys are not affected (key_leaf maps -0.0 to 0.0). Proposed DESIGN sentence for L1.17: two floats of one value and one format order -0.0 before 0.0, as IEEE totalOrder and min/max do. Then change the ignored test l01_17_value_representation::edges::the_two_float_zeros_tie_in_the_natural_order to expect Less and remove its ignore. Not unsound: no Zed program at L1 observes the natural order of non-key floats (no sort word; min/max have their own IEEE rule). Deferred tests: /home/luke/Work/wt/scratch/deferred-tests/SPEC-zero-order.rs, back into `tests/steps/l01_17_value_representation/edges.rs` when this step is done. | - | - | none |  |

The checker accepts no program where an `int` reaches such a last arm (a decimal or a `/` removes `int` from the class, L1.26a), and the kernel has no operation on an `int` and another carrier nor `/` on two `int`s, so elaboration lays the two operands out on the patterns of the one whose last arm is at the other carrier `c` (`f64` for `/` on two `int`s), each taking its value at `c` in the new last arm (`elab::walk::without_int`, O(C²) per operation, C ≤ 4, arms moved, not copied); no value is given that the checker did not give. `x * (1 / 2 + 2 ^ 2 + 1)`, `x * ((1 + 1.5) + 0)` and `x * (1 / 2 + 0)` are one `match` (`FOLDED`), and `1 / 2 - 0` and the mutants of `(1 + 1.5) + 0` are skipped. Benches: the sum of quotients 7.95 times (128.9 to 1,024.3 million instructions at 2,000 and 16,000), the chain 8.00 times. Found by STAGE-generic-fold-div: an operation on generic literals alone whose last arm, at `int`, mixes carriers is still a `let` and a `match` per following literal: `x * (1 / 2 + 2 ^ 2 + 1)`, where `1 / 2` is a `rat` and `2 ^ 2` an `int` in that arm, and `x * ((1 + 1.5) + 0)`, a decimal and an integer. The value is unchanged, but the L25.8 mutation skip does not see the form folded, and in `x * (1 / 2 + 0)` the mutant `1 / 2 - 0` is reported undetected rather than skipped, since the build stage cannot build `int / int` in that arm (the kernel has no `/` on two `int`s). Fix: the checker gives those literals a carrier's value in the last arm, as it gives `1.0` in `x == 1 / 2`, or elaboration drops the last arm where the checker proves no `int` reaches it; test in `l01_26a_generic_literals::operations` (`NOT_FOLDED`) and `l25_08_mutate::examples::a_mutant_of_a_folded_decimal_or_power_is_skipped` | - | - | STAGE-generic-fold-div |  |

Cause (traced by walk-next2, 2026-11-16, on 4d45d6d19, profiling zedc, `--report run`): the check stage alone is 250M, 941M, 3,676M and 14,663M instructions at n = 50, 100, 200 and 400 (4.0 times per doubling; elaboration 8M to 276M, also above linear, cause inferred to be the same). A count at `replay`'s call in `Ck::apply_one` (walk.rs) shows `h{i}`'s signature holds i + 1 needs, all `NeedKind::Map { f }`, a chain on m, R0, R1, … each giving the next, and `replay` leaves none (`left` empty): `meet` sends each need back through `map_end` on the bound type, a variable of the caller, which records it again as a new need of the caller. So each link meets every need below it, about 190k instructions each (250M / 1,250 at n = 50; 14.66G / 80,200 at n = 400): O(n²) in all, from the size of the signatures, not from a stray loop. The needs are distinct, so no merge of equal needs helps. DWARF call graphs did not unwind past the leaf frames here (Zen 3: no LBR), so the trace is from the count, not a call-graph profile. Build (hard algorithm: solve, then cross-review before merge): a forwarding need, kept where every need of the callee would only become a need of the caller, as one need "calls `h{i-1}` with (F, M), gives R" holding the callee's `Arc<Sig>`, expanded only where a call binds F; O(1) needs a link and O(n) at the call that binds `f`. It reaches each `NeedKind` match (about 220), the needs readers in zedc-stage, zedc-presburger and the elaborator, and the repair chain of MSG-forwarded-repair; it needs a proof that expanding later meets the same needs with the same results as meeting them at each link. Expected: the chain checks in O(n) or O(n log n); ratio under 10.5, under 9 preferred. Trial rule: no admission while `trying`; `touch` under `trying` forces before it takes its snapshot (mod.rs); a need that hits a deferred key copies with no undo entry. | 0 | FAIL-arrow-lambda-partial-slot | Open after arrow-slot (2026-11-16, 0cbb40ab4, which did MSG-arrow-lambda-rebuild-repair only). Findings: DESIGN (sec:type_resolution rule 2, "checked once per arrow"; rule 6 picks the arrow at each call) accepts both programs and gives 8, so the refusal is a gap of zedc, not of the language. One closure body cannot choose the test, since the test depends on the arrow the caller picks and function values carry no run-time type; the elaborator has no machinery for intersections of arrows (each lambda is one `Term::Lam`, built once per span). Two routes, both larger than M: (1) elaborate a value of an intersection of function types to one function per arrow (Dunfield, "Elaborating intersection and union types", JFP 2014): a lambda at an intersection is built once per arrow, a call through such a value takes the one rule 6 chose, and every place a value meets an intersection or one arrow of it builds or projects; (2) a function value carries its exact domain at run time and the partial-slot rebuilding (`in_domain` in crates/zedc-elab/src/elab/walk.rs) tests that domain; this agrees with the static types because an exact arrow refuses a wider function (probe: `wide(x: int \| f64)` passed as `(x: int) -> int` is refused with "Try `pick(g: x -> wide(x: x))`"), but it changes `Term::Lam`, the kernel's closures and native code. Until then the refusal names the lambda and the intersection and offers the lambda once at each arrow, which runs. Found by twice-proof (2026-11-16) while doing PROOF-twice-lambda-placement. A lambda passed at an intersection of function types is checked once for each arrow (`Ck::fit_step`), and the elaborator builds each span once with one fit. With `small(x: int) = x + 1; small4(x: f64) = 2; apply(f: (x: int \| f64) ->? int) = f(x: 2.5) else 6; pass(x) = apply(f: x); both(h: ((g: (x: int) -> int) -> int) & ((g: (x: f64) -> int) -> int)) = h(g: small) + h(g: small4);`, both `a = both(h: g -> pass(x: g))` and `a = both(h: g -> apply(f: g))` need a test of `int` at `g` for one arrow and of `f64` for the other. Before 5400e8605 the first stopped a debug build on the assertion in `Ck::coerce_at` and the second was accepted and ran `small` on 2.5 ("a bug in zedc itself"); since then both are refused (`a_lambda_checked_at_each_arrow_is_rebuilt_once`). By the language's rules both give 8. Do: make them run, for instance by elaborating such a lambda once per arrow, or by a domain test read from the function value at run time; then replace the refusal cases of that test. Steps (Codex R6): (1) freeze the encoder's specification for recursive types and write its bottom-up DAG form (open: equivalence across every shortcut of `Key::order` is the claim most likely wrong); (2) exact encodings of every leaf, with `Rat` as separate numerator and denominator residues and a zero marker (Gemini R5's residue drops a prime base equal to the sampled prime, R6-X2) and `Big` likewise; (3) audit every constructor and shortcut that can make two equal keys by different paths (open for the whole kernel); (4) measure the node layout (+1 word); (5) change the three priority sites (set, list, settings) together; (6) check cost and output; (7) restate K123 and `priority.rs`. | 70 | FFI-sandbox-linux | DESIGN step L7.4e (sec:ffi "A restricted library", author P244, P248; study SANDBOX-study, notes /home/luke/Work/wt/sandbox-study/notes.md): `with restrict(read:, write:, network:, processes:)` on the result type of each function that gives an isolated library's token; requires `isolate: true`; deny by default once written; the same facts on every token-giving function of a library. The wrapper sets no_new_privs, then a Landlock ruleset (ABI 6 for any restrict, 9 for `write:` with paths, 10 for `network: #outbound`; the loader closure read and map only, the channel, and under a network grant the six name-lookup files in /etc read-only), then a seccomp filter (the fixed floor: ptrace, mount, namespaces, BPF, keyring, io_uring, abstract sockets; listen and accept under `#outbound`, since a kernel-bound socket listens past Landlock's bind rule; clone and execve under `processes: #none`), all returning EACCES or EPERM, never killing; then dlopens the library. A host below the ABI the values need gives `#ioError(op: "restrict", path:, why:)` at the start. The four sec:diagnostics rows (not isolated, two ways, target cannot enforce, relative path), each with its repair compiling; `zedc ports` prints the facts; a denied open, connect, listen, exec gives the errno in the library; negative control with the seccomp listen rule removed; scaling of setup in the number of paths | M | yes | FFI-isolate | `crates/zedc-check/src/check/`, `crates/zedc/src/`, `crates/zed-rt/src/`, `../libzed/`, `tests/steps/l07_04e_restricted_ffi/ (new)` |

Was: `l01_23_subtyping::witnesses::periodic_lists_agree_with_their_lengths` failed at `ZED_TEST_SEED=16903030027676086283` (about 1 fresh seed in 300; spawn-queue line 876, diagnosis by bundle-pres2): `greedy_length` in zed-kernel `types/empty.rs` (COMPLEXITY K34) missed a length that exists, so a list type the rule finds inhabited drew `Refused(NoWitness)`. Cause, confirmed: the choice by conditional expectations counted the expected number of classes alone, in `f64`, which can exceed one when the shares sum to exactly one, and tied on `none = [(3, 1), (6, 1), (3, 0), (6, 2)]`, taking the length 0, which `(3, 0)` holds. Fix: a pessimistic estimator (Raghavan 1988) less one meeting pair (Hunter 1976's bound on a tree of one edge), counted exactly in integers, whose expectation starts below one whenever the rule finds a length and never rises, so a length is found whenever the rule finds one (proof at `greedy_length`); each prime's least residue found on the tree of the classes modulo its powers. Departs from the proposed fix, a search over residues with backtracking, metered: that search is exponential in the primes and needs a meter, this one is polynomial, exact and needs none. Tests: the seed as a fixed-seed test, `empty::tests::a_length_is_given_when_two_classes_taken_out_meet_and_their_shares_sum_to_one` (control: without the pair it fails), the scan of up to four negated classes requiring a length wherever the rule finds one, and the benchmark `witnesses::bench::a_list_of_cycles_less_many_scales` (8.15 at 7.97 times the definitions). | S | yes | none | `crates/zed-kernel/src/types/empty.rs`, `crates/zed-kernel/src/types/empty/`, `tests/steps/l01_23_subtyping/` |

Was: Found by FP-ops-concat-zip (2026-11-16): `a.zip(b)` is accepted only when each operand's sure keys hold the other's possible keys (`zip_end` in `crates/zedc-check/src/check/walk/fp_ops.rs`), so a zip whose equal counts the program shows but the types do not is refused as undecided (DESIGN: an undischarged assertion is a static error): `m.stdin.zip(m.stdin)`, `m.stdin.zip(m.stdin.map(f))`, and `ys = xs.map(f); xs.zip(ys)` for an `xs` of computed length; `xs.zip(xs.where(p))` is rightly refused. Decided by call-zip-design (2026-11-17, zed 2857e44): DESIGN sec:joins "What proves two keyspaces equal" and the test L5.2 names. A key-set name on the type is unsound, confirmed by probe at zed-impl e09d73852: with `read(n: int) = (0 ..< n).map(i -> i * 2)`, `xs = read(n: m.args.count)` and `ys = read(n: m.args.count + 1)` both print as `int ->? int` and have 0 and 1 entries when run with no argument; `xs.zip(ys)` is refused, rightly. Work, in the checker: a union-find of keyspace classes, one class for each binding, each call evaluation and each port read; `.map(f)` and `zip` give their operand's class; two ranges whose ends are the same names or literals share a class; `0 ..< x.count` takes the class of a list `x`; an `if` or `match` gives its branches' class where all agree, else a new one; a loop's generation variable keeps its `initial` value's class where every update keeps the class of the step before (checked once, by induction), else a new class per generation; in a body each parameter has its own class, a `zip` of two parameters becomes a need checked at each call (rule 4 of sec:type_resolution), and a signature records the parameter whose keys the result keeps (one optional index; a recursive function's record is assumed, then kept only where the body gives it; a value that may hold several functions keeps it only where they all agree). Also: a range `0 ..< e`, where `e` is `x.count` or a `min` with `x.count` among its operands, has its keys within `x`'s, so `x[i]` there has no `#outOfBounds` and the offered repair `(0 ..< min(xs.count, ys.count)).map(i -> (xs[i], ys[i]))` has no failure member. Tests: those of L5.2 (accepted: the three zips above, a mapping loop, a branch `if c { xs } else { xs.map(f) }`, `pairUp(xs, xs.map(f))`; refused: the two `read` calls, `xs.zip(xs.where(p))`, `if c { xs } else { ys }`, a filtering loop, `pairUp(xs, ys)`, `[1, 2].zip([1])`); the repair's type. Scaling: O(n α(n)) for n bindings, call evaluations and port reads, timed at n and 8n. `Sig` (crates/zedc-types/src/ty.rs) has a hand-written equality (`Same`) and a digest-based hash, which the new field must enter; 35 lines construct `Sig {` literally (grep at e09d73852; an earlier note said about 69). | L | no | none | `crates/zedc-check/src/check/walk/fp_ops.rs`, `crates/zedc-types/src/ty.rs`, `tests/steps/l03_15a_fp_ops_run/` |

## File conflicts at the same level

Each pair below is at one level, shares a file and is not yet done. No path of needs joins two items at one level, since each level is one more than the highest level among the item's needs. Under the rule of 2026-11-02 the two may run in parallel and the merge resolves the overlap; run them apart where possible. There are 5125 pairs. This section and the next are written by `cargo run -q -p zed-tools --bin conflicts` from the items table above (with `--check` it only compares them with it); edit the table and rerun it, not the lists. Two items share a file when a path of one equals a path of the other or lies inside a directory path of the other, one that ends in `/`. Paths are compared as written, less a trailing ` (new)`; files under `tests/` and the files every step touches are not compared. The two items of a row are in the order of their rows in the table, and the shared paths are the longer path of each match.

## Machine limits and tools

The author installed the tools below on 2026-11-02. Each was run that day on a small input, and the versions are the ones reported. All tests stay under 60 s each and 112 GB in total. There are two test suites. The local suite, `tools/run_tests.sh`, needs only the Rust toolchain and the cores of the machine, and it is what CI runs: tests in `tests/steps/`. The full battery, `tools/run_tests.sh --full`, is the local suite plus `tests/full/<step>/`, each with a file `needs` listing its tools. It stops before any test and names what is missing, so nothing is skipped. `tools/fetch_test_deps.sh` fetches into `~/.cache/zed-test-deps`, with no root, what Fedora does not package: target sysroots, the official rustc for target builds, and Podman's test storage and image. Every test that uses a tool in this table goes in `tests/full/`, and a step with such tests runs `--full` before it merges. Plain `cargo test` does not build `tests/full/`; clippy in CI compiles it.

| Items | Tools and what was run | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| L21.1, L21.3 | PostgreSQL 18.6 (`initdb`, `pg_ctl`, a query), MariaDB 11.8.8 (`mariadb-install-db`, `mariadbd` as `mysqld`, a query), SQLite 3.51.2. | Run private instances as the user, in a temporary directory, on a socket with networking off. Do not use the system services. |
| L26.1 | `wasmtime` 50.0.1 from cargo, in `~/.cargo/bin`, which must be on `PATH`. Ran a module built with `clang --target=wasm32` and `wasm-ld`. | Use `wasmtime` for the cross-target tests. |
| L27.1 | RTX 3050, driver 615.78.08, Vulkan 1.4. `llvmpipe` software Vulkan is also present. | Run the GPU tests on the card locally. `llvmpipe` gives a software device where no GPU exists. |
| L27.2 | Multi-host behavior runs on one machine. Rootless Podman 5.8.9 with `crun` 1.28: two containers on a private network reached each other, and `podman kill` (0.1 s), `pause`, and `network disconnect` and `connect` worked. A paused container's processes stop, but its kernel still answers ping, so a pause test must watch the protocol, not ping. A container starts in 1.5 s. A veth pair between user network namespaces with `tc netem` delayed packets, which needs no root. KVM (`/dev/kvm`, `qemu-system-x86_64`) is also present. | Each node is a rootless Podman container, with the storage from `tools/fetch_test_deps.sh`. Stopping a machine is `podman kill`, pausing one past its lease is `podman pause`, a partition is `podman network disconnect`. Delay and loss use `netem` on a veth pair. Use a KVM VM only for what a container cannot show, such as a kernel crash. Do not use Docker. |
| L27.3 | Yosys 0.67 (synthesis of a small module), Verilator 5.046 (lint), Icarus Verilog 13.0 (simulation). | Use these. |
| L28.1, L28.2 | `mlir-opt`, `mlir-translate`, `llc`, `opt` and `wasm-ld`, all LLVM 22.1.8, matching `clang`. Lowered a small module from MLIR through `llc`. | Use these. |
| L29.1, L29.2 | `qemu-aarch64` and `qemu-riscv64` 10.2.2, `clang`, `lld`, and gdb 18.1, which reads both targets. With the sysroots from `tools/fetch_test_deps.sh`, C, C++, static C and Rust programs ran under qemu on both targets, gdb stopped at a breakpoint through `qemu -g`, and `zed-rt` built for aarch64 with the official rustc 1.99.1. | Link with `~/.cache/zed-test-deps/bin/<arch>-cc`, run with `qemu-<arch> -L ~/.cache/zed-test-deps/<arch>/usr/<arch>-linux-gnu`, and build target Rust with `~/.cache/zed-test-deps/rust/bin/rustc`. Fedora's rustc rejects the official target std with E0514. `tests/full/s00_01_tools/` shows each command. |
| L30.1, L30.6 | `code`, node v22, `Xvfb` and `xvfb-run` (ran a command under `xvfb-run`). | Run headless editor tests under `xvfb-run -a`. |
| L5.14, L23.5 | Timing runs must not share the 32 cores with other branches. | Run these alone, with no parallel branch active. |
| L7.15 | The 10 GB demo must fit the 112 GB and 60 s caps. | Size the run to fit, and report the size used. |
| L19.3 | The run takes over 60 s. | Split it per program. |
| XE2 | Codex and `agy` logins; `agy`'s three environment variables. | Running now. If a login fails, report it. |

CI has none of these tools and runs only the local suite, so each item in this table puts the tests that use them in `tests/full/`. Timing tests can fail when other work loads the machine (5 pieces failed at load 57 on 32 cores and passed when rerun alone), so read a failure under load by rerunning the piece before calling it a regression.

## Why each item waits

- **T2-eval.** No needs. *Note:* on_stack is called at product.rs:1281,1508,1637 and preimage.rs:170,2204,2225,2294, so removing it touches product.rs; do that part after ST1 or keep on_stack as a thin no-op until T2-mid deletes it. Keeping the no-op wrapper is the recommended way to avoid an edge to ST1 and ST2. *Note:* MAX_DEPTH was the hidden limit set by the thread stack. It is gone: DESIGN.md sec:kernel clause (i) now has no nesting limit, and the operations on `Value` and `Family` hold their depth on the heap (repair T2-eval-repair).
- **T3.** No needs. *Note:* Must precede L1.40 by user order (item 3); no technical tie. Stale TODO: Z8 is marked fixed at COMPLEXITY.md:111 and tables.rs has port_at; the stopped patch holds const_at and lambda_at. Confirm const_at and lambda_at are in tables.rs before starting (the row says so; I read only the port_at part). What is really open is Z9: visit clones each node at tables.rs:106,109, and NodeInfo owns node and alone: Region. The cheaper fix may be a borrowed Tables<'a> or Arc-shared regions in zir, not imbl; imbl is not a zed-native dependency yet. The patch also holds an unrelated `early` condition release for if in codegen.rs; check whether that landed before deleting it.
- **T4.** No needs. *Note:* Must precede L1.40 technically as well as by user order (items 4, 9): HC4 narrowing runs through Scope::reduce and project into this solver, and L1.40's scaling numbers would measure the cubic cost otherwise. Edits outside presburger.rs are the callers of a new refusal error: today callers use Over (product.rs:1201,1238, preimage.rs:267-289, hull.rs), and a refusal needs a variant and a diagnostic row, plus DESIGN text for that error. So T4 goes before ST1 and ST2 on product.rs. Cross-review (no-thresholds, hard-algorithms rules) is needed only if no bound is found without it; if it is needed, add an edge from XE2 or a separate round. Fix the stale comment at scaling.rs:93 here, since T10 would otherwise edit the same file.
- **LR1.** No needs. *Note:* Algorithm is in ../squirrelparser/paper/squirrel_parser.tex fig. Code: memo entry with inRecPath, foundLeftRec and a per-position version; expansion loop; never replace a match by a mismatch. Zed specifics: memo key is (rule, pos, head), so the version per position must cover both head values; `expected` and `far` keep the failures of the last failed expansion, since that pass reaches the operator a flat `*` loop stops at and dropping them would lose operators from the messages (the aim, unchanged tests/steps/l01_08_parser/errors.rs, holds; see STATUS.md); a re-match leaves dead nodes in the arena (linear, acceptable). Paper's quadratic case: lookahead over a left-recursive rule at every position. The grammar's lookaheads `&('{' Item)` at syntax.peg:138 and `!(Name ':') Expr` at :123 need a scaling test after LR2. Must precede LR2, T2-parse and L2.1. Shares no file with L1.40, so can run alongside it.

- **S.1h.** S.1: the Zed0 subset settled and the catalog rerun over current Rust. *Note:* Added 2026-11-09 by the author's order that the Zed compiler be statically unable to stop on a broken assumption of its own: every check the Rust compiler makes at run time on its own state, with a crash on failure, becomes a fact the Zed checker proves at compile time. Not in scope: rejecting user programs and reporting failed file reads and writes, which answer the program and its inputs. Feeds S.2, whose slice is the first to port listed checks.
- **STRICT-build.** STOP-switch: the explicit stops and `--allow-stops`. L18.2b: the `preallocated` mode whose bounds the switch demands. L16.1: `@assume`. With `x: int[lo..]`, `x::min` is the tree of `lo`; `Small::constraints.written` holds the tree of `x * x < 100`; `Small::constraints.subject` is the tree of `x`; on `n: int where n + m == 10`, `n::constraints.relations` holds that relation's tree. With `x: int`, `x::max == #unbounded` and `x::min == #unbounded`; with `x: int[0..]`, `x::min` is 0 and `x::max` is `#unbounded`; a program that matches on `x::max` and does not narrow `x` builds. `T::shape` of a refined string carries its constraints in member `#string`, and an unrefined string carries none.

The `Ref` member goes into S.1b's `Ast`, which is the reason for the edge to S.1b. *Test added 2026-11-05:* (a) With a recursive `fib` called on a run-time argument, the `::ast` tree of the caller reaches `fib`'s `::ast` tree; a run-time value depending on that tree is a staging error, and one depending on the `::source` reference compiles. (b) A foreign function declared by signature gives name and `::shape` only. (c) A call of a local lambda gives no tree. (d) One selected arrow gives a `#reference` with one `Ref`, and a two-unit order follows the unit's qualified name. (e) Batch and single-file checks give the same trees. (f) With `twice(positional f: (rat -> rat), positional x: rat) = f(f(x));`, the tree of `((x: rat) -> twice(square, x))::source` reaches `twice`'s tree, its `f(x)` nodes give no tree, and the argument `square` is a reference giving `square`'s tree.
